summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Work centers on hardware-aware model optimization and AI/ML benchmarking: 8-bit quantization cutting GPU memory ~55% at under 1% accuracy loss, TensorRT inference delivering a 5.2x speedup, and custom CUDA C++ kernels beating naive GPU convolution by ~35%. Builds training and inference pipelines in Python, C/C++, and PyTorch across heterogeneous compute, from GPU accelerators to embedded processors on Linux.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free visual document understanding transformer, on a custom medical billing dataset for structured field extraction.
Built preprocessing and training pipelines in PyTorch with the HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder API, adding domain-specific special tokens and resizing the decoder embedding layer.
Improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% through improved preprocessing and model tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 annotated images achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for deployment under constrained-hardware budgets.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones on BraTS 2020 multi-modal MRI; evaluated on Dice Score and IoU and reported accuracy-latency trade-offs for deployment.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency using pynvml and psutil.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC with under 1% accuracy degradation and a +0.09 perplexity increase.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights and biases, and preallocated global buffers.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU TorchScript, a ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built automated data generation pipelines in the CARLA simulation environment using semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering, producing ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18) for an adaptive control stack.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO achieving a 5.2x inference speedup (56.7 → 10.9ms; 17.6 → 92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for real-time visual servoing.
Deployed across heterogeneous compute elements, pairing a Jetson GPU accelerator with an Arduino embedded processor over a unified WebSocket fabric.
